title: Particles, isotopes and relative atomic mass; Mass spectrometry of elements; The mole and Avogadro constant; Ionic bonding and lattices
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: AS01#t2 term and clue written for the game; AS02#t2 term and clue written for the game; AS02#t1 term and clue written for the game; AS02#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AM01#N.3a, AS01#N.5a, AS02#N.6a, BD01#N.3a, AM01#N.5a, AS01#N.7a, AS02#N.10, BD01#N.6, AM01#N.8a, AS01#N.15, AS02#N.13, BD01#N.12a.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Mass number
items.clue: The total count of protons and neutrons in a nucleus, symbol A.

items.label: Mass-to-charge ratio
items.clue: The quantity written m/z, plotted on the x-axis of the spectrum.

items.label: Mass spectrometer
items.clue: Instrument that turns particles into positive ions and sorts them.

items.label: Relative abundance
items.clue: Shown by peak height: how much of each isotope an element contains.

questions.stem: How many atoms are there in 0.500 mol of water, H₂O? (N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)
An ion X³⁺ contains 23 electrons and 30 neutrons. Which nuclear symbol represents this ion? (Each symbol is written with its superscript first and its subscript second.)
questions.explanation: Protons = 23 + 3 = 26 = Z. Mass number = 26 + 30 = 56. (X is iron.)

questions.stem: The mass spectrum of element E shows three peaks from singly charged atomic ions: m/z 24 (relative abundance 100), m/z 25 (relative abundance 12.7) and m/z 26 (relative abundance 13.9). What is the relative atomic mass of E, calculated from these data?
An atom of element X has the electron configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁴. Which ion does X form in its ionic compounds?
questions.explanation: Six outer electrons (3s² 3p⁴). X gains two to reach 3s² 3p⁶: 16 protons, 18 electrons, charge 2−. X is sulfur: S²⁻.

questions.stem: A student writes: 'Mr of carbon dioxide, CO₂ = 44.0 g mol⁻¹'. Which comment on this statement is correct?

options.text: It is correct: Mr and molar mass are one and the same quantity.
The unit is wrong: Mr is the mass of one molecule in grams.
The unit is wrong: Mr is measured in atomic mass units.
The unit is wrong: Mr is a ratio of masses, with no unit.

questions.explanation: Mr compares a CO₂ molecule with 1/12 of a carbon-12 atom; units cancel. M(CO₂) = 44.0 g mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: Chlorine (atomic number 17) has isotopes with mass numbers 35 and 37. Pure samples of ³⁵Cl₂ gas and ³⁷Cl₂ gas are compared at the same temperature and pressure. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The ³⁷Cl₂ gas diffuses more slowly than ³⁵Cl₂.
The two gases diffuse at the same rate as each other.
The two gases undergo different chemical reactions.
The ³⁷Cl₂ molecules contain more electrons than ³⁵Cl₂.

questions.explanation: At the same temperature the heavier ³⁷Cl₂ molecules move more slowly on average. Diffusion rate is a physical property.

questions.stem: The electron-impact mass spectrum of a liquid has peaks at m/z 15, 29, 31, 45 and 46, plus a very small peak at 47. Which compound could it be? (Aᵣ: H 1.0, C 12.0, O 16.0)
questions.explanation: Mᵣ = 2(12.0) + 6(1.0) + 16.0 = 46.0, matching M⁺ at 46. The tiny 47 peak is M+1.
One Ca²⁺ (2+) is balanced by two OH⁻ (2 × 1−). The bracket keeps each hydroxide ion whole.

questions.stem: How many ions are there in 5.55 g of calcium chloride, CaCl₂? (N_A = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹; Ar: Cl 35.5, Ca 40.1)
Bromine's relative atomic mass is 79.90, almost exactly halfway between 79 and 81. What does this show?

options.text: Most bromine atoms are bromine-80, with 45 neutrons each.
Every bromine atom has the same mass, 79.90, between those of its two isotopes.
Bromine is a mixture of bromine-79 and bromine-81 atoms in roughly equal numbers.
Bromine's electrons add 0.90 to the mass of each bromine-79 atom.

questions.explanation: 50.7% ⁷⁹Br and 49.3% ⁸¹Br weight the two masses almost equally: (78.918 × 50.69 + 80.916 × 49.31) ÷ 100 = 79.90.

questions.stem: The mass spectrum of gallium shows two peaks from 1+ ions: m/z 69 (height 100) and m/z 71 (height 66.4). What is the relative atomic mass of gallium given by these data?
Sodium chloride has a very low volatility: it does not evaporate at room temperature and melts only at 801 °C. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: Every ion is strongly attracted to many ions of opposite charge.
Its particles are so heavy that they cannot move fast enough to escape.
Evaporating it would break the strong bond in every NaCl molecule.
Sodium is a metal with a high boiling point, and NaCl keeps this property.

questions.explanation: Each ion is surrounded by oppositely charged ions and attracted to all of them. Separating them means overcoming many strong attractions.
